Agricola: Why Is Another Person More Than Another Action?

A farm can contain rooms, fields, and animals. The design problem is how these things produce decisions. Why might taking more wood now postpone construction? Why can gaining a worker make the next harvest more demanding?

This article uses the two-player base rules of Agricola’s 2016 revised edition, separately from the 2007 edition, solo rules, and the variant without hand cards. Lookout’s revised-edition page identifies the edition and designer Uwe Rosenberg. Our three situations are independently constructed local examples, not playtest reports or the book’s examples. Hand cards remain unplayed, with no special effects changing these resolutions. You can compare the situations without knowing the whole game first.
Angle one: a growing pile still offers only one opportunity to take it

Placing a person on a shared action space both provides an action and makes that space unavailable for the rest of the round. Untaken goods on accumulation spaces remain when the next round adds more. The amount available therefore depends on when someone takes it. Base rules, page 6

Suppose the work phase of round six is nearly over. Lin and Jo each have two family members, one already placed and one remaining. Lin places next, followed by Jo’s final person. Both farms have six wood, two reed, two wooden rooms, and an empty space orthogonally adjacent to a room. Forest and Farm Expansion are unoccupied; Forest contains six wood. Earlier actions have no further effects.

Compare these two specified sequences. Whoever expands builds only one wooden room, with no stable; whoever chooses Forest takes all six wood. The new room costs five wood and two reed. Appendix, pages 6–7
Sequence · Lin at the end of the round · Jo at the end of the round
Lin takes Forest; Jo expands · 12 wood, 2 reed, 2 rooms · 1 wood, 0 reed, 3 rooms
Lin expands; Jo takes Forest · 1 wood, 0 reed, 3 rooms · 12 wood, 2 reed, 2 rooms

Neither branch adds a person. Lin cannot take six wood and then build with the same person, or treat Jo’s occupied space as a queue still available to join. Both players subsequently return their people home. Round six has no harvest. During the next preparation, the emptied Forest receives three wood. In a different situation where nobody took the six wood all round, the next addition would instead bring it to nine.

There is no changing posted price for wood here. Rather, how much one placement brings back competes with what one placement can construct. More wood does not mean more developed farm space, and a new room does not arrive with a new person. Jo’s actions are specified choices for the comparison, not predictions of a real opponent.

When designing a shared action board, record the benefit, the duration of occupation, and the benefit’s later use separately. Calling a space “take resources” can conceal how its first visitor changes someone else’s opportunities. Renaming wood for a different setting will not by itself change that relationship.
Angle two: additional labor starts paying off after its first feeding cost

Set up a separate two-player situation late in round seven. Lin has two people, three wooden rooms built legally earlier, and five food. Lin has one person left to place; Jo has finished all placements. Basic Wish for Children and Day Laborer are both unoccupied. Lin has no crops, animals, or other food-providing effects. Compare through this harvest, then count the people available next round.

If Lin chooses family growth, a third person is placed beside the person taking the action; Lin declines the optional minor improvement. The newborn takes no further action this round. After returning home, the two existing people require two food each and the newborn requires one: all five food are used. Next round Lin can place three people in turn.

If Lin chooses Day Laborer, two food are gained, taking the supply from five to seven. The family still has two people, requiring four food, so three remain. Next round there are still only two people to place. Growth and feeding: rulebook pages 7 and 9; Day Laborer: appendix page 6
Choice · Does this placement add another action this round? · Food after harvest · People available next round
Family growth · No · 0 · 3
Day Laborer · No · 3 · 2

The benefit is an additional action next round, not consecutive turns or guaranteed access to a preferred space. At the following harvest, this person, now participating in work, ordinarily requires two food. If only the initial food changes from five to four, the growth branch is one food short at this harvest, taking one begging marker worth minus three points at the end. Having enough room and having enough food are different conditions.

This does not establish that growth should be avoided. It shows why an investment needs at least three points on a timeline: the action committed now, the first opportunity to use its output, and the first maintenance payment. Recording only “two people become three” misses both the two food Lin declined to gain and the additional feeding requirement. Looking only at the food left over misses the future choices.
Angle three: the order of harvest decides whether two sheep can leave a third

Now compare the round-nine harvest of another two-player game. Lin has two existing family members and two sheep in one fully fenced pasture covering two farm spaces. It has no stable and a capacity of four. A Fireplace was legally built and paid for earlier. There are no crops, other animals, or relevant card effects. Only the starting food differs: state A has two, state B has four. Use the same policy in both: cook only the sheep needed to cover this feeding, then retain the animals.

There are no crops to collect in the field phase. Feeding follows, requiring four food for two people. In A, the Fireplace converts one sheep into two food; the resulting four food are all paid. In B, the existing four food are paid without cooking a sheep. The one-sheep-to-two-food conversion is visible on the Fireplace illustration on rulebook page 10.

Only then do animals breed. A has just one sheep left, so cannot breed: it finishes with one sheep and no food. B retains two and has room for their offspring, gaining one sheep: it finishes with three sheep and no food. Neither receives a begging marker.

Two additional food did not directly buy two sheep. They preserved one existing animal and maintained the pair needed for breeding. Conversely, A cannot borrow an anticipated newborn to feed the family first. Breeding happens after feeding, and cooking parents or offspring during the breeding phase is expressly prohibited. Harvest sequence, rulebook page 9

Rooms, food, and sheep make it easy to bring farm expectations to the table. Resolution still depends on the objects, capacities, and timing this game specifies. The people are being fed here; do not invent a daily fodder cost for sheep. More sheep also need not immediately mean more endgame points: without additional scoring cards, one sheep and three sheep both score one point in the sheep category. We compared growth conditions and retained resources, not whole-game winners.
A development account: why not one birth for every pair?

The appendix’s development credits say Hagen Dorgathen identified runaway growth from breeding per pair or per pasture during early development. They also describe using card-play records to revise overly strong and weak cards. This is the rulebook’s development retrospective, not our balance experiment; the credits attribute the current rulebook’s writing to Rosenberg. Appendix credits, pages 10–11

The current rules cap each animal type at one offspring per harvest. Maintaining the condition for reproduction is therefore different from multiplying the production rate without limit. In your own growth system, you could vary the number of producers, output per event, and frequency separately, then record successive results. The credits supply neither a complete earlier ruleset nor comparative testing data, so that proposed experiment should not be presented as the designer’s documented method.
Check your understanding
After taking the six wood from Forest, can Lin immediately build using the same person? No. That placement resolves Forest. Another action requires a person and an available space.
Does the third person gained in round seven act again that round? No. The action benefit starts next round, while this round’s harvest already requires one food for the newborn.

Why can two more food before harvest leave two more sheep afterward? They preserve one parent and thus keep the two-sheep breeding condition satisfied; the subsequent breeding supplies the additional sheep.
Editions and sources
Lookout: Agricola, Revised Edition 2016: edition, designer, and revision information. The examples exclude old-edition and solo exceptions.
English base rulebook: pages 6–10 for actions, growth, harvest, and the Fireplace; page 12 for ending and edition-specific exceptions.
English appendix: pages 6–7 for action names and values, pages 10–11 for development credits, and page 11 for sheep scoring thresholds. PDF page positions and printed numbers coincide.
Can’t Stop：同一把骰子，为什么越走越难停？
掷出骰子以后，你还能选择怎样配对；棋子走了一段以后，你还能选择现在停手。但这两个决定并不独立：先前选了哪些列，决定下一掷有哪些数字可用；本回合已经走了多远，决定失败时要放弃多少进度。《Can’t Stop》把这两种选择放在同一段行动里。
本文采用 Ravensburger 2007年版、编号26 434 6的基本规则，不加入规则书末尾的三种变体。该版支持2—4人，目标是先赢得三列。下文两个两人局面均为本站自行构造，用于追踪决定的后果，不是试玩记录，也不是完整游戏教学。规则书由 Ravensburger 编写，链接为标明获发行商许可的镜像。规则书第1、4页
角度一：可以重新配对，但不能重新分配三枚棋子
四颗骰子分成两对，各对的和指定一列。三枚白色棋子记录本回合的临时进度；用完以后，就只能推进已经进入的列。选定配对后，能执行的两对都要执行，但基本规则允许有意选择只能推进一枚棋子的配对。规则书第2页
先看局面甲。两人都没有赢得任何列，所以全部列仍开放。轮到小岚，她先前停手保存的位置是5列第1格、7列第2格、9列第1格；其余列没有她的棋子。经过本回合前几次掷骰，三枚白棋现在分别在5列第3格、7列第4格、9列第2格，已经全部用完。对手的保存位置是2列第1格、8列第2格、11列第1格，其余为空。
所有格数从底部第一格向上数，不在列中记为0。小岚这次掷出 1、2、4、6。把四颗骰子各用一次，只有以下三种配对结构：
配对与两对的和 · 本局面能执行什么 · 执行后的白棋位置（5、7、9列）
1＋2、4＋6 → 3和10 · 两列都没有白棋，也没有空闲白棋；不可选来推进 · 不产生合法移动
她可以选第二行或第三行；不能把9列的白棋拿去8列，也不能同时取第二行的5和第三行的7，因为那会重复使用骰子。未被执行的另一对，不会积存到下一掷。
两种合法选择都只增加一格，但增加在哪一列仍由她决定。此时限制选择的，不只是骰面，还包括已经占用的三枚白棋。对设计师而言，这是一种可以检查的承诺：早先选的路线，后来仍在约束行动。若允许每次掷骰后随意搬动白棋，同样的骰面便能不断开启新列，先前选列的约束会减弱；这是一个需要另行测试的改法。
角度二：停手保存的是本回合进度，失败也只退回保存处
在局面甲中，小岚选择推进5列，白棋变成4、4、2。她现在面对停手或再掷一次。许可方 franjos 的官方玩法概述也强调了这一循环：继续尝试，或者结束本回合并留下可在以后接续的位置。此概述用于交叉核对基本机制，具体结算仍以本文选定的2007年规则为准。
若现在停手，小岚把自己的保存位置更新成5列第4格、7列第4格、9列第2格，收回三枚白棋，交给对手开始下一回合。没有一枚到达列顶，本局仍未有人赢列。
若她继续，假设下一掷是 1、1、1、1：怎样分组都只有2和2，三枚白棋却在5、7、9列，而且没有空闲白棋可放。她不能执行任何移动，回合立即失败；白棋移走，保存位置仍为1、2、1，对手的所有棋子不变。规则书第3页
这次失去的进度可以逐列核算：
列 · 回合开始前已保存 · 再掷前的临时位置 · 若失败，损失的本回合格数
因此，失败不是把累计10格全部清空，而是放弃尚未保存的6格。反过来，停手也不能只保存5列、让其余白棋接着掷；这里结束的是整个回合。把风险对象写清楚，才能知道玩家实际在作什么决定。
还要区分“更舍不得失败”和“下一掷更容易失败”。只要三枚白棋仍在5、7、9列且都未到顶，多走一格不会改变四颗公平、独立骰子的分布，也不会改变哪些数字能让至少一枚白棋移动；增加的是本回合尚未兑现的进度。不能因为刚连续成功几次，就说下一次失败已经被“攒出来”了。
这个案例可迁移到带撤退决定的探险原型：先给每次失败画出它会回退到的准确位置，再让玩家比较多走一步与现在兑现。若把每一步都立即保存，损失边界消失，这里的停手理由也会随之改变。至于玩家是否觉得紧张，应当通过试玩观察，不能由这张表直接宣布。
角度三：长短不同的列，让收获同时改变赛场
该版棋盘的2列只有3格，7列有13格，都包含顶端目标格。短列所需步数少，却不意味着下一掷更容易推进它。规则书第1—2页棋盘图
本站独立穷举了四颗公平、相互独立六面骰的1296种有序结果：至少能挑出两颗凑成2的有171种，约13.19%；至少能凑成7的有834种，约64.35%。这里只问一掷中“有没有这样一对”，尚未检查白棋是否可用、列是否开放，也没有计算完成整列的概率。路线长短与出现机会不同，是要一起比较的两个条件；这组数值没有证明各列价值相等。
再看独立的局面乙。仍为两人局，尚无任何列被赢得。小岚保存的位置是5列第1格、7列第11格、9列第1格，其余为空；她的三枚白棋已在本回合走到5列第2格、7列第12格、9列第2格。对手保存的位置是5列第1格、7列第10格、9列第1格，其余为空。
小岚掷出 1、1、2、6。两枚1彼此配对得到2和8，均无法推进；各自与2、6配对则得到3和7，可以把7列白棋从第12格推进到第13格。两枚1的身份互换不会产生新的数字选择。
这时，7列仍未被小岚赢得。她若继续，顶端白棋不能再移动，也不能拿去开新列；只有5、9列白棋还可推进。假如随后掷出四枚1，同样只能得到2和2，她本回合失败，7列保存棋子仍在第11格，对手第10格棋子也仍在。登顶这一掷没有提前兑现。
若小岚在登顶后停手，保存位置改成5列第2格、7列第13格、9列第2格；她赢得7列，对手在7列的保存棋子被退还。此后双方都不能再进入7列。小岚只赢了一列，游戏继续；赢得第三列时才立即结束。规则书第4页
为了看清封列的作用，让对手下一回合掷 3、3、4、4。现在只能使用6和8，在这两列第1格各放一枚白棋，第三枚仍空闲；7和7因为封列不可用。如果从封列前、对手7列仍保存于第10格的局面作比较，同样骰面还允许选择7和7，把一枚白棋推进到第12格。这里消失的是一个可选去处，不能说这一掷必然失败。
因此，一列的完成有两层后果：增加自己的胜利进度，同时撤掉所有人今后能使用的一条路线。对手已经保存的进度虽能抵挡自己回合失败，却不能抵挡别人先赢得该列。设计竞赛目标时，可以分别检查“我拿到什么”和“别人因此还剩什么可做”。本文是在解释这些规则如何共同工作，没有把这一解释当作 Sid Sackson 本人的创作动机。
带答案的自查
局面甲掷出1、2、4、6，能同时推进5和7吗？不能。两种和属于不同配对，不能重复使用同一颗骰子。
小岚白棋在4、4、2时继续并掷出四枚1，累计进度全部归零吗？不会。保存位置仍为1、2、1，丢掉的是本回合增加的6格。
局面乙7列白棋刚到第13格，对手的第10格棋子立即被清走吗？没有；小岚停手赢得该列时才清走。若继续后失败，双方原有保存位置都保留。
7列封闭后，对手掷3、3、4、4就一定失败吗？不一定。本例三枚白棋都空闲，仍可选择6和8，分别从第1格开始。
规则与发行商来源
Ravensburger：Can’t Stop!，2007年，编号26 434 6：第1—4页基本规则；第4页变体不采用。PDF为发行商编写的规则书，托管于 brettspiele-report。
brettspiele-report：规则书镜像出处：“Spielanleitung”部分注明获得 Ravensburger 许可；仅用于说明文件出处。
franjos：Can’t Stop 官方介绍：“Das Spiel”部分交叉核对四骰配对、三枚临时棋子及保存进度；该页当前商品图片不用于替代2007年版规则。
Can’t Stop: Why Does the Same Handful of Dice Become Harder to Put Down?

After rolling, you can choose how to pair the dice. After advancing, you can choose to stop. These decisions are connected: the columns chosen earlier determine which numbers remain useful, while this turn’s accumulated progress determines how much a failure would cost. Can’t Stop puts both decisions inside one sequence of actions.

This analysis uses the Ravensburger 2007 base edition, product number 26 434 6, excluding its three variants. It supports two to four players; the first to win three columns wins. Both two-player situations below were constructed for this article to trace consequences. They are neither playtest records nor complete instructions. Ravensburger authored the rulebook; the linked mirror states that it hosts the rules with publisher permission. Rulebook, pages 1 and 4
Angle one: you can change the pairing, but cannot reassign your three runners

Divide four dice into two pairs; each sum identifies a column. Three white runners track temporary progress this turn. Once all are placed, only their columns remain available. Use both pairs when the chosen pairing permits it, but these base rules allow choosing a pairing that advances only one runner. Rulebook, page 2

Consider situation A. Neither player has won a column, so all columns remain open. It is Lan’s turn. Her banked positions are space 1 in column 5, space 2 in column 7, and space 1 in column 9; she has no markers elsewhere. After earlier rolls this turn, the white runners stand at spaces 3, 4, and 2 in those columns. All three runners are in use. Her opponent’s banked positions are space 1 in column 2, space 2 in column 8, and space 1 in column 11, with no other markers.
Count spaces upward from the bottom, starting at 1; absence from a column counts as 0. Lan rolls 1, 2, 4, 6. Using each die once gives three pairing structures:
Pairing and sums · What this situation permits · Resulting runner positions in columns 5, 7, 9
1 + 2, 4 + 6 → 3 and 10 · Neither column has a runner, and none is available to enter; this cannot supply a legal move · No legal movement
1 + 4, 2 + 6 → 5 and 8 · Advance column 5 once; no runner can enter column 8 · 4, 4, 2
1 + 6, 2 + 4 → 7 and 6 · Advance column 7 once; no runner can enter column 6 · 3, 5, 2

Lan may choose the second or third row. She cannot transfer the column 9 runner into column 8. Nor can she take the 5 from one pairing and the 7 from another: that would reuse a die. The unused pair is not stored for a future roll.

Both legal choices add just one space, but Lan still chooses where it goes. Her options depend on the occupied runners as well as the dice. This gives a designer a concrete kind of commitment to inspect: a route chosen earlier continues to constrain later actions. Allowing runners to move freely between columns after every roll would let the same dice keep opening new routes, weakening that commitment. That would be a proposed change requiring its own test.
Angle two: stopping banks this turn’s progress; failure returns to the banked positions

In situation A, Lan advances column 5, leaving runners at 4, 4, and 2. She can now stop or roll again. Licensor franjos’s official overview also describes this cycle of continuing or ending a turn with positions that can be resumed later. It corroborates the core mechanism; the selected 2007 rulebook governs the detailed resolution here.

If Lan stops now, her banked positions become space 4 in column 5, space 4 in column 7, and space 2 in column 9. The runners come off and pass to her opponent for the next turn. None reached a summit, so neither player has won a column.

If she continues, suppose the next roll is 1, 1, 1, 1. Every pairing produces 2 and 2. Her runners are in columns 5, 7, and 9, and none is available to enter column 2. No movement is possible, so her turn immediately fails. Remove the runners; her banked positions remain 1, 2, and 1. All opposing markers stay where they are. Rulebook, page 3
Account for the lost progress column by column:
Column · Banked before this turn · Temporary position before rerolling · This turn’s progress lost on failure
Total · 4 · 10 · 6

Failure does not erase all ten accumulated spaces. It discards the six spaces that remain unbanked. Conversely, stopping cannot bank only column 5 while leaving the other runners in play: the whole turn ends. A precise loss boundary tells us what decision the player is actually making.

Also distinguish “more progress to regret losing” from “a greater chance of failure on the next roll.” While the runners remain in columns 5, 7, and 9 and none has reached the top, another space of progress does not change the distribution of four fair, independent dice, or which numbers can move at least one runner. It changes the unbanked progress at stake. A run of successes does not accumulate a failure that must arrive next.

For an exploration prototype with a retreat decision, mark exactly where each failure would return the player, then compare another step with banking now. If every step were banked immediately, this loss boundary would disappear and the reason to stop would change. Whether participants experience tension still requires observation in play; the table cannot establish that response.
Angle three: columns of different lengths make a reward change the race

On this edition’s board, column 2 has three spaces and column 7 has thirteen, including their numbered summit spaces. Fewer required steps do not imply a better chance of advancing on the next roll. Board diagrams, rulebook pages 1–2

Our independent enumeration of all 1,296 ordered outcomes of four fair, independent six-sided dice found 171 outcomes containing some pair totaling 2, about 13.19%, and 834 containing some pair totaling 7, about 64.35%. This asks only whether such a pair exists in one roll. It does not check runner availability or closed columns, and is not the probability of completing a whole column. Route length and the opportunity to roll its number are different conditions to compare; these figures do not establish equal column values.

Now consider the separate situation B. Again, two players are playing and nobody has won a column. Lan has banked space 1 in column 5, space 11 in column 7, and space 1 in column 9, with no markers elsewhere. This turn’s runners have reached spaces 2, 12, and 2 in those columns. Her opponent has banked space 1 in column 5, space 10 in column 7, and space 1 in column 9, with no other markers.

Lan rolls 1, 1, 2, 6. Pairing the two ones gives 2 and 8, neither usable. Pairing them separately with 2 and 6 gives 3 and 7, allowing the column 7 runner to move from space 12 to space 13. Exchanging the two identical ones produces no new numerical choice.

Lan has not yet won column 7. If she continues, that runner cannot advance farther or move to another column; only the runners in 5 and 9 can still move. If she then rolls four ones, the resulting 2 and 2 cause failure. Her banked column 7 marker remains at space 11, and her opponent’s remains at space 10. The summit roll did not bank itself.

If Lan instead stops after reaching the summit, she banks spaces 2, 13, and 2 in columns 5, 7, and 9. She wins column 7, and her opponent’s marker in that column is returned. Neither player may enter it again. Lan has won only one column, so play continues; winning a third ends the game immediately. Rulebook, page 4

To isolate the effect of closure, let her opponent roll 3, 3, 4, 4 at the start of the next turn. The usable choice is now 6 and 8: place one runner on space 1 of each column, leaving the third available. The 7-and-7 pairing is unusable because that column is closed. For comparison, before closure, with the opponent still banked at space 10 in column 7, the same dice would also allow 7 and 7, taking one runner to space 12. An option has disappeared; this roll has not become an automatic failure.

Completing a column therefore has two consequences: it advances the winner’s objective and removes a route from everyone’s future play. Banked progress survives a player’s own failed turn, but not someone else winning that column first. When designing a race objective, inspect both what the winner receives and what others can still do afterward. This is our analysis of how these rules work together, not a claim about Sid Sackson’s personal design intentions.
Check your understanding
In situation A, can 1, 2, 4, 6 advance both columns 5 and 7? No. Those sums belong to different pairings and would reuse a die.
With runners at 4, 4, 2, does continuing into a roll of four ones erase all Lan’s progress? No. Her banked positions remain 1, 2, 1; the six spaces gained this turn are lost.

In situation B, does reaching space 13 immediately remove the opponent’s marker at space 10? No. Removal happens when Lan stops and wins the column. Continuing into failure preserves both players’ original banked positions.
After column 7 closes, must 3, 3, 4, 4 cause her opponent to fail? No. All three runners are available in this example, so 6 and 8 can each receive a runner on space 1.
Rules and publisher sources

For Sale：买到最好的房子，为什么还可能少赚？
你加价抢到最大的数字，下一阶段也拿到最大的支票，最后却可能输给提前退拍的人。这里需要分清三件事：拿到什么房子、出售时排第几，以及这一来一回留下多少钱。
《For Sale》由 Stefan Dorra 设计。本文选用 IELLO 2020 年英文 V2 基本规则；发行商产品页列出的该版发售日为2020年7月10日，不把它当作游戏最初问世的年份。IELLO 官方产品页
下面三个局面由本站自行构造，不是试玩记录或作者自述。金额统一以千元为单位：现金5代表5,000元，房子上的5只是排序数字。我们关注的是：先付现金取得手牌，再把手牌按相对名次换成收入，会怎样改变决定？
角度一：退拍既支付成本，也改变下一人的退路
基本版买房时，每次亮出与人数相同的房子。顺时针轮到一人，他可以加价或退出；退出者拿走尚余房子中数字最小的一张。本版取回已出价金额的一半，取回数向下取整；坚持到最后的人取得最后一张，并支付全部出价。英文规则第4—6页
设三人按甲、乙、丙顺时针坐好，首轮由甲开始。每人现金28，没有房子或支票。桌上公开4、17、29号房，未来牌堆不公开。出价过程为：甲1、乙3、丙5、甲加到6。甲这次补5，累计出价为6；不是再加6变成7。随后乙退出，丙也退出。
玩家 · 本轮最后出价 · 取回／实付 · 得到房子 · 剩余现金
乙退出时，最小房子是4；乙拿走它以后，丙的退出所得才变成17。退出不只是“我不玩了”，它还会把别人的保底结果往上推。甲成为下轮先手。此例在买房轮结束时停止，不能把29直接折算成29千元，也还没有出售收入。
甲最后比丙多付3，拿到更高的房子，但这3是否值得，要等出售时面对的支票和其他人出牌才能判断。丙也不是完全免费离场：出过5后退出，损失的是3。若误把“实付的一半”向下取整，就会把丙写成只付2，低估继续参与的代价。
对设计而言，值得检查的是退出的三个后果：谁还能行动、退出者拿到什么、留下的人接下来面对什么。三人最终各得一张牌，竞争改变的是牌的排序能力与现金余额；“没有赢下最高价”并不等于“本轮没有得到东西”。
还要分开公开出价与可隐藏的余额。桌上能核对甲已经出6，却不必直接看见他还留了多少现金；本例写明每人的28，是为了复算。若在原型中改成完全公开余额，可以观察人们怎样判断对方还抬得动多少，不能直接断言竞价因此就没有悬念。规则第3、5页
角度二：房子的数字不标售价，只决定这一批的名次
出售时，支票先公开，每人暗选一张房子，全部选好后一起亮出，按房子从大到小对应支票从大到小；用过的房子离开游戏。英文规则第8—9页
另设一个三人局，买房已结束，出售只剩两轮。为让读者复算，列出全部余牌、现金和此前收入；这些记录不表示桌上始终公开所有手牌与金额。买房归属曾经公开，但本轮选的是哪张，要到共同亮牌时才确定。
玩家 · 剩余房子 · 现金 · 已收支票总额
当前支票为2、10、15。甲已经暗选24，比较两种同时亮牌的结果：
分支 · 三人亮牌（甲／乙／丙） · 三人收入（甲／乙／丙）
同一张24，在第一支排第一，在第二支排第三，相差13。它没有固定卖价；比较的是当前对手实际投入的牌。玩家可以记得别人买过27、30，却不能仅凭持有记录确定他们这一轮会不会用。
继续把两条分支算完：固定最后一批支票为0、7、14，到下一轮才公开。第一支余牌是6／27／30，第二支是6／12／18；各人只剩一张，均按甲／乙／丙取得0／7／14。现金加全部支票后，两支终值分别为94／83／95和81／91／100，都是丙获胜，且没有并列。
这不是让甲预知尾批的策略建议。我们固定后续，只为隔离“同样出24，别人换牌会怎样”。本轮差13并不等于整局领先13；此前收入、剩余现金以及用掉哪些房子，都还在账上。想把同时选择用于自己的设计，可以检查：玩家能看到当批奖励吗？承诺后还能改牌吗？别人改变的是我的合法行动，还是同一行动的收益？
角度三：现金变成一次性手牌后，购买力不能原样回来
最后看一个从末次买房算到终局的对照。三人买过九轮，各剩现金8，已有房子如下；最后未售出的房子为3、16、28，甲先行动。
表中手牌和现金供读者核算。桌上当批房子与出价公开；未来支票没有预先展示，也没有谁能在看完别人的出售牌后再挑自己的牌。
玩家 · 已有九张房子
本轮再次出现甲1、乙3、丙5、甲6，乙退出，取回1、支付2，拿走3，现金剩6。现在轮到丙，比较两个合法分支：
丙的选择 · 甲的结果 · 丙的结果
退出 · 全付6，得28，余2 · 取回2、付3，得16，余5
加到7，随后甲退出 · 取回3、付3，得16，余5 · 全付7，得28，余1
丙从退出改为加价，多付4，把16换成28。甲退出后不再有下一次出价，丙立即按最后留下者结算。所有房子此时分完，买房阶段结束。
为了单独检查这4的效果，构造两条相同的后续：大家都把刚买的牌留到最后，其余九张以同一组合法出牌和支票批次出售，甲、乙、丙分别累计取得70、70、69。最后公开4、12、13，三人只剩刚买的那张，必须一起亮出。这个后续是分析条件，不是买房时已知的未来。
分支 · 最后一轮收入（甲／乙／丙） · 终局总额（甲／乙／丙） · 胜者
丙的高牌确实多卖1，却多花4，个人终值减少3。这里无需假定对手犯错：我们检验的是一组指定行动的后果，没有证明丙退出在所有后续中最优。若最后两张较高支票的差额改变，或这些房子更早投入别的批次，比较也会改变。
现金与房子在流程中承担不同任务。现金能参加后续买房，未花掉的部分还会计入最终财富；房子进入手牌后，只能在一次出售中交出，不能拿收到的支票返回买房。三人基本局用完30张房子，每人买十张、卖十次，所以多花钱通常不会增加出售次数，而是改变手中各次出牌能争的名次。规则第2—4、6、8、10页
这是本站对两阶段衔接的解释：做资源转换设计时，要分别检查数量、用途、退出系统的时点和终局价值。“钱换牌”只说出转换方向，还没有说清玩家究竟多得到几次行动，还是同样次数中的更强选择。
基本牌的房子1—30各不重复，亮牌不会出现房子数字并列；支票金额可以重复，相同金额分给相应名次即可。终局金额若相同，比较未花现金，仍相同则共享胜利。上面两个完整结尾都不需要用到破同分规则。规则第2、10页
带答案的自查
第一例丙出价5后退出，要付2还是3？付3，取回的是向下取整后的2；乙先拿4，所以丙取得17。
第二例甲用24，能保证拿15吗？不能；对手亮27和30时，24排第三，只拿2。
第三例丙多付4得到28，最后也拿了最大支票，为什么终值反而少3？因为这条指定后续只多收入1，1－4＝－3；较高支票不能单独证明整局更划算。

For Sale: Why Can Buying the Best House Leave You with Less?

You bid for the biggest number and later collect the biggest check, yet someone who passed earlier can finish richer. Three different results need separating: which house you acquire, where it ranks when sold, and how much money the exchange leaves you.

For Sale was designed by Stefan Dorra. This article uses IELLO’s 2020 English V2 base rules. Its product page dates this edition to July 10, 2020; that is not the game’s original publication year. IELLO’s official product page

All three situations below are our constructed examples, not playtest records or the designer’s account. Money is measured in thousands: cash of 5 means $5,000; House 5 is a ranking number. The design question is: what changes when cash first buys a hand of cards, and those cards later earn money through relative rank?
Angle one: passing pays a cost and changes the next player’s fallback

In buying, a round offers one house per player. Players act clockwise, raising or passing. A passer takes the lowest remaining house and recovers half their bid, rounding the recovered amount down. The last bidder pays everything bid for the last house. English rules, pages 4–6

A, B, and C sit clockwise in that order, with A starting the first round. Each has 28 cash and no houses or checks. Houses 4, 17, and 29 are public; future decks are hidden. A bids 1, B bids 3, C bids 5, and A raises to 6. A adds 5 to reach a total of 6, rather than adding another 6. B then passes, followed by C.
Player · Final bid this round · Recovered / paid · House received · Cash left

When B passes, the smallest house is 4. Only after B removes it does C’s fallback become 17. Passing does more than end someone’s participation: it improves the next remaining player’s fallback. A starts the next buying round. This example stops at the auction’s end. House 29 is not $29,000, and no selling income has arrived yet.

A paid 3 more than C for a higher house. Whether that difference pays off depends on later checks and the cards opponents commit. C did not leave for free either: passing after bidding 5 costs 3. Rounding the payment down instead of the refund would incorrectly make that cost 2.

For a design review, examine three consequences of withdrawal: who can still act, what the departing player receives, and what the remaining players face next. Everyone here receives one card. Competition changes their ranking strength and cash balances; failing to win the highest house does not mean receiving nothing.

Public bids also differ from cash balances, which may be hidden. Everyone can verify A’s bid of 6 without directly seeing the cash left behind it; this example states each starting 28 for calculation. In a prototype with fully public balances, observe how people assess an opponent’s ability to raise. Do not assume this change must remove suspense. Rules, pages 3 and 5
Angle two: a house number sets a rank within this batch, not a sale price

In selling, checks are public before everyone secretly selects a house. All selections are revealed together, with descending house ranks matched to descending checks. Sold houses leave play. English rules, pages 8–9

Consider a separate three-player game with buying finished and two selling rounds left. The table gives readers the complete remaining hands, cash, and previous income for calculation. It does not make all those holdings permanently public at the table. Acquisitions were public, but this round’s commitments are revealed together.
Player · Remaining houses · Cash · Checks already collected
The current checks are 2, 10, and 15. A has committed 24. Compare two simultaneous reveals:
Branch · Houses A / B / C · Income A / B / C

The same 24 ranks first in one branch and third in the other, a difference of 13. It has no fixed sale price: the comparison uses the opponents’ actual commitments. Remembering that they acquired 27 and 30 does not establish that they will spend them now.

Finish both branches with the final checks fixed at 0, 7, and 14, revealed only next round. Remaining hands are 6 / 27 / 30 in branch one and 6 / 12 / 18 in branch two. With one card each, A / B / C receive 0 / 7 / 14 in both. Adding cash and all checks gives final totals of 94 / 83 / 95 and 81 / 91 / 100. C wins both, without a tie.

This is not advice based on A knowing the final batch. Fixing the continuation isolates what happens when opponents change cards against the same 24. Earning 13 more now does not mean leading the game by 13: earlier income, remaining cash, and consumed cards still matter. In a design with simultaneous choices, examine whether current rewards are visible, whether commitments can change, and whether another player changes your legal action or the return on that same action.
Angle three: cash becomes a supply of cards that can each be used once
Now compare two paths from the final buying round to the end. After nine buying rounds, each player has 8 cash and these houses. The final houses offered are 3, 16, and 28, with A acting first.

Hands and cash are listed for readers’ calculations. The current houses and bids are public; future checks have not been shown, and nobody can wait to see opponents’ selling cards before choosing their own.
Player · Nine houses already held
Again, bids are A 1, B 3, C 5, A 6. B passes, recovering 1 and paying 2 for House 3, leaving 6 cash. C must now act. Compare two legal branches:
C’s choice · A’s result · C’s result
Pass · Pay all 6; receive 28; keep 2 cash · Recover 2, pay 3; receive 16; keep 5 cash
Raise to 7, then A passes · Recover 3, pay 3; receive 16; keep 5 cash · Pay all 7; receive 28; keep 1 cash

By raising rather than passing, C pays 4 more to replace 16 with 28. Once A passes, there is no further bidding opportunity: C settles as the last player. Every house has now been distributed, ending buying.

To isolate those extra 4, construct the same continuation in both branches. Everyone saves this newly acquired house until the final sale. The previous nine houses are sold through an identical legal sequence of commitments and check batches, earning A, B, and C totals of 70, 70, and 69. Finally, checks 4, 12, and 13 appear. Each player has only the newly acquired card to reveal. This continuation is an analytical condition, not knowledge players had while bidding.
Branch · Final sale income A / B / C · Final wealth A / B / C · Winner

C’s higher card really earns 1 more, but costs 4 more, reducing C’s final wealth by 3. This calculation need not assume an opponent made a mistake: it examines specified actions without proving that passing is best across every continuation. A different gap between the final two highest checks, or using these houses in earlier batches, would change the comparison.

Cash and houses serve different purposes. Unspent cash remains part of final wealth; checks cannot reopen the completed buying phase. In this three-player base game, 30 houses give everyone ten purchases and ten sales. Paying more changes the strength of a commitment within that supply, rather than adding another sale. Rules, pages 2–4, 6, 8, and 10

Our interpretation of this connection suggests four separate design checks: quantity, permitted uses, when something leaves the system, and final value. “Money becomes cards” names a conversion, but does not yet distinguish extra actions from stronger choices within the same number of actions.

Houses 1–30 are unique, so house ranks cannot tie. Check values can repeat, yielding equal payments at those ranks. Equal final wealth is broken by unspent cash, then shared victory. Neither completed example needs that tiebreaker. Rules, pages 2 and 10
Check your understanding
In example one, does C pay 2 or 3 after passing on a bid of 5? 3: the recovered amount is rounded down to 2. B already took 4, so C receives House 17.
Does playing House 24 in example two guarantee the 15 check? No. Against 27 and 30, it ranks third and receives 2.

Why does C finish 3 poorer in example three despite paying 4 more for 28 and taking the biggest final check? That specified continuation adds only 1 income: 1 − 4 = −3. A larger check alone does not prove a better whole-game return.

El Grande：人数没变，为什么先后和去向会改变影响力？
地图上放着不同颜色的骑士，似乎只要数谁最多就能理解局势。但在《El Grande》里，骑士从哪里来、何时能入场、何时才能决定去向，会一起改变这个比较。本文用三组独立局面，观察人数之外的设计关系。
范围固定为 Hans im Glück 2023 英文规则的四人基础游戏，使用四至五人那面地图；不加入小扩展、老手替换牌、两人替身或短局。作者为 Wolfgang Kramer 与 Richard Ulrich，版本可由出版社页面和规则核对。以下局面、比较与判断为本站构造，不是作者的测试记录，也不是整局攻略。
为避免名称混淆：Caballeros 是参与人数比较的骑士；Court 是玩家面前的个人供应；Province 是尚未调来的公共供应。Castillo 指立体城堡，Castilla 则是地图上的一个地区。
角度一：抢到先选权，也可能让手边补给更少
先给林一个很具体的机会。四人游戏第1轮，大家各有7名骑士在 Court、21名在 Province，另有2名在各自起始地区。乔、梅、博依次公开打出11、8、4号权力牌，最后轮到林。林可以出13，也可以出9；都没有与本轮已出的数值重复。五张行动牌已经公开，其中包括可部署5人的 Your Majesty，以及可部署3人的 Fiesta。
这次只跟踪林的供应与城堡投入量。约定谁选 Your Majesty 都不移动国王；林若选 Fiesta，也不执行它的特殊计分。其他人的后续行动不改变林的骑士。两条分支分别如下：
林的选择 · 行动顺序与牌的去向 · 林的补给 · 林的部署 · 林行动后
打出13 · 林先行动，选 Your Majesty · 不从 Province 调人 · 向 Castillo 投入5人 · Court剩2人；本轮投入5人
打出9 · 乔先选走 Your Majesty；林随后选 Fiesta · 从 Province 调2人，Court变9人 · 向 Castillo 投入3人 · Court剩6人；本轮投入3人
9号牌的2人补给、12／13号不补给，以及部署只能来自 Court，见规则第4—6页。这里没有把“权力9”当成9名骑士，也没有把行动牌上的部署上限当成凭空得到的人。
比较结束时，林在13号分支投入城堡的人更多，却少留下4名可以等待以后部署的骑士。这4人的差额有两个来源：少调来的2人，以及本轮多投入的2人。牌上的数值因此不是一个统一的“实力值”；它连接了先后、可选行动与个人供应三个不同环节。
这也不证明9一定更经济。我们写定了乔会取走 Your Majesty，林才失去这个选项；若乔选择别的牌，后手未必付出同样代价。当前城堡局势、其他行动牌和后续轮次，都会改变林需要什么。可迁移的设计问题是：让玩家为先选权付出代价时，代价发生在现在的补给、未来的手牌，还是此刻放弃的行动上？应分别列账，不能只把大数字称为“强牌”。
角度二：同一张牌的两个动作，顺序会改变合法地点
换一场刚开始的四人游戏。国王在 Castilla，林的 Grande 和2名骑士在 Galicia，林的 Court 有7人。乔、梅、博的起始地区分别为 Navarra、Toledo、Sevilla。林打出13，最先选择 Your Majesty。现在只看林这一次行动，其他玩家尚未行动。
这张牌让林可以部署至多5人，并移动国王。Castilla 与 Galicia 相邻，但国王所在地区不能接收骑士。林比较两个完整顺序：
顺序 · 第一步 · 第二步 · 林的骑士分布
先部署，后移动国王 · 从 Court 向 Galicia 放5人 · 把国王移到 Galicia · Galicia有7人，Castilla为0；Court剩2人
先移动国王，后部署 · 把国王移到 Galicia · 从 Court 向相邻的 Castilla 放5人 · Galicia有2人，Castilla有5人；Court剩2人
两边国王最终都在 Galicia，林投入人数也完全相同，留下的局面却不同。第一条分支先完成增援，再使该地区进入不能更改的状态；第二条分支先改变了哪些地方允许部署，因此不能再把那5人放进 Galicia。规则第5—6页；Your Majesty 说明见第12页
林不能先放2人、移国王、再放3人：两个动作各自必须完整做完。国王的移动也不是骑士从一个地区走到另一个地区；这两种移动对象不能混用限制。
这里改变的是其他玩家下一次行动时面对的合法选项。第一条分支的7人不会因此立即得分，也没有永久占有权；国王以后还可能被移动，后续计分仍须看当时人数。若教区域争夺时只展示最终颜色和数量，就会漏掉“这块地方现在能否被改变”这一层。
设计自己的位置规则时，可以先选定两个动作，在纸上分别走完两个顺序。比较的重点不只是收益加起来是否一样，还包括中间一步有没有改变下一步的进入资格、目标对象或可选范围。顺序本身已经能产生取舍，不一定要再添加一种资源。
角度三：城堡里的人数，与他们将去哪里，是两种不同的不确定
再换一个独立局面：第3轮结束，准备第一次总计分。国王在 Granada。林、乔、梅、博的 Grande 分别在 Toledo、Aragón、Cataluña、Sevilla；Galicia 与 Navarra 没有 Grande，也没有改分牌。城堡此前的公开投入合计为林2人、乔2人、梅1人、博0人。这里把总数写给读者看，方便核算；玩家不能为了确认数量而临时打开城堡。
城外与本例有关的骑士如下。其他地区不受这次目的地选择影响；本例只统计城堡及这两个地区的本次得分，不把它当整局总分。
计分前地点 · 林 · 乔 · 梅 · 博 · 第一／二／三名的基础分
大家先秘密设定目的地，再打开城堡计分，最后将各自城堡里的骑士整组移往所选地区，之后才给地区计分。因而选目的地时，不能等看见别人去哪里再跟着修改。规则第6—8页
林把2人投向 Galicia，梅把1人投向 Navarra；博城堡里无人，本例设他的转盘指向 Toledo。现在只改变乔的选择，其余前提不动：
乔的目的地 · Galicia迁入后的人数及得分 · Navarra迁入后的人数及得分 · 连同城堡的三处得分合计
Navarra · 林3、乔2：林4分、乔2分 · 林1、乔3、梅2：林1分、乔5分、梅3分 · 林8、乔10、梅4、博0
Galicia · 林3、乔4：林2分、乔4分 · 林1、乔1、梅2：林1分、乔1分、梅5分 · 林6、乔8、梅6、博0
城堡的得分在两条分支都一样：林与乔并列最多，各得第二档的3分，梅得第三档1分。第二条分支的 Navarra 中，林与乔并列次位，所以各得第三档1分。人数为0不会仅因排名空缺而得分。两处目的地都没有国王或 Grande 奖励。并列与奖励规则，第8页
乔把2人改投 Galicia，确实从林手中拿走该地区的领先，但乔在这三处的合计反而从10变8。与此同时，梅没有改变决定，却从4变6。这说明多人多数制的影响会跨地区转移：一个地点上的胜负，不能替代对整组结算的比较。这里仍没有证明乔在整局中该选哪边；未来布局及其他得分都没有被简化成这个小表。
城堡还把“记住过去的公开投入”与“猜测别人现在的秘密选择”放在了一起。即使林准确记得每种颜色有几人，也不能由此知道乔的转盘。做自己的隐藏信息组件时，应分别决定哪些信息可以追溯、哪些决定尚未揭示，以及承诺发生在何时。透明容器可以减轻记忆负担，却不会自动消除秘密选目标的判断；这是本站提出的可测试改法，不是本游戏的变体或作者已验证的结论。
设计者记录：换主题时，保留什么、重新组织什么？
在2015年 Brettspielbox 访谈中，Kramer 回顾与 Ulrich 开发的“特洛伊木马”项目遇到同题材作品后，如何寻找新的主题。他说他们判断自己的机制仍有区别，因此继续在既有机制上开发，转向西班牙背景。访谈引述的作者轶事也明确提到，主题与游戏系统都作了改变。
这份记录支持一个具体的开发经历，不支持“只要换名称就完成了换主题”。同样，它没有交代本文两个国王行动顺序如何被设计出来，也没有提供透明城堡的对照测试。把记录与本站分析分开后，我们才可以继续问：新主题中的角色、动作和关系，分别帮助玩家理解了哪些规则，又有哪些地方仍需要明说？不要把历史背景中的常识直接当作行动权限。
带答案的自查
林出9并调来2人，是否能不经过 Court 就从 Province 部署更多人？不能。行动牌的部署数量是上限，实际可用者仍来自 Court。
最后都是国王在 Galicia、共部署5人，为什么两个分支不同？国王移动的时点改变了部署时的合法地区；两个动作也不能拆开交错。
记得城堡里每种颜色的数量，是否就知道本次区域得分？不知道。秘密目的地还未揭示，迁入又在地区计分之前。
上表中乔赢得 Galicia，是否意味着乔这三处合计更多？不是。乔从10变8，必须连同 Navarra 的损失一起算。

El Grande: Why Do Order and Destination Change the Value of the Same People?

A map full of colored knights can look like a straightforward counting problem. In El Grande, where those knights come from, when they may enter, and when their destination becomes fixed all shape that count. Three independent situations let us examine the relationships behind the numbers.

This article uses the four-player base game in Hans im Glück’s 2023 English rules, on the four-to-five-player side of the board. It excludes the mini expansions, alternative cards, two-player dummy and short game. The publisher’s page identifies Wolfgang Kramer and Richard Ulrich as the designers. Our situations and comparisons are original analysis, not their test records or a strategy guide to an entire game.

Caballeros are the knights counted for majorities. The Court is a player’s personal supply; the Province holds those not yet recruited. Castillo means the physical castle. Castilla is a region on the map: they are different places.
Angle one: Earlier access can come with less supply in hand

Consider Lin’s first round in a four-player game. Each player has seven Caballeros in their Court, twenty-one in the Province and two in their starting region. Jo, Mei and Bo have publicly played Power cards 11, 8 and 4, in that order. Lin plays last and can choose 13 or 9 without duplicating an earlier value. The five Action cards are already face up, including Your Majesty, which permits five placements, and Fiesta, which permits three.

We track Lin’s supply and castle contributions. Whoever chooses Your Majesty declines to move the King. If Lin selects Fiesta, Lin declines its special scoring. The others’ subsequent actions do not change Lin’s Caballeros. Compare these specified sequences:
Lin’s card · Order and Action card · Recruitment · Deployment · After Lin’s turn
13 · Lin acts first and takes Your Majesty · None from the Province · Five into the Castillo · Two remain in Court; five contributed this round
9 · Jo takes Your Majesty first; Lin then takes Fiesta · Two from the Province, making nine in Court · Three into the Castillo · Six remain in Court; three contributed this round

The two recruits on card 9, zero on cards 12 and 13, and the separation between Court supply and deployment are grounded in rules pages 4–6. A Power value of nine does not mean nine recruits. A placement allowance does not create the people to fill it.

With 13, Lin has contributed more to the castle but retains four fewer people for later deployment. That difference combines two forgone recruits with two additional placements. The large number on the Power card therefore connects three separate things: timing, available actions and personal supply. It is not a single measure of strength.

Nor does this prove that 9 is always more efficient. We specified Jo’s choice. If Jo takes another action, acting later might not lose Lin access to Your Majesty. The castle situation, other available actions and future rounds could all change what Lin wants. For a design of your own, separate the price of earlier access into its parts: current supply, future card options and the action forgone now. Calling the largest number “the strong card” hides that work.
Angle two: Two actions on one card can change each other’s legal targets

Start a different four-player game. The King is in Castilla. Lin’s Grande and two Caballeros are in Galicia, and Lin has seven in Court. Jo, Mei and Bo start in Navarra, Toledo and Sevilla respectively. Lin plays 13 and chooses Your Majesty first. We examine this one turn before anybody else acts.
Lin can deploy up to five Caballeros and move the King. Castilla and Galicia are adjacent, but the King’s own region cannot receive Caballeros. Here are two complete orders:
Order · First action · Second action · Lin’s resulting position
Deploy, then move the King · Place five from Court in Galicia · Move the King to Galicia · Seven in Galicia, none in Castilla; two in Court
Move the King, then deploy · Move the King to Galicia · Place five from Court in adjacent Castilla · Two in Galicia, five in Castilla; two in Court

Both branches end with the King in Galicia and the same five people deployed. In the first, reinforcement happens before Galicia becomes protected from changes. In the second, moving the King changes the legal deployment targets, so those five cannot enter Galicia. Rules pages 5–6; Your Majesty on page 12

Lin cannot place two, move the King and then place three: each action must be completed before the other begins. Moving the King is also a different operation from moving Caballeros between regions. Their restrictions cannot be interchanged.

The difference changes the options available when the others take their turns. Seven in Galicia do not score immediately or grant permanent ownership. The King can move later, and a later scoring considers the position then. A lesson about area competition that shows only final colors and quantities misses another question: can this place currently be changed?

For your own rules, choose two actions and work through both orders. Compare more than the sum of their rewards. Does an intermediate step change eligibility, the kind of object that can be targeted, or the set of possible destinations? Sequence can create a decision without adding another resource.
Angle three: How many are in the castle and where they will go are different uncertainties

Now consider an independent position at the end of round three, just before the first general scoring. The King is in Granada. Lin, Jo, Mei and Bo have their Grandes in Toledo, Aragón, Cataluña and Sevilla respectively. Galicia and Navarra have no Grandes or scoring tiles. Announced contributions to the castle total two for Lin, two for Jo, one for Mei and none for Bo. We give the reader these totals for calculation; players cannot open the castle simply to check their memory.
The relevant positions are below. The other regions are unaffected by these destination choices. Our subtotal covers the castle and these two regions at this scoring, not a complete game score.
Before scoring · Lin · Jo · Mei · Bo · Base points for first / second / third

Players commit to destinations before the castle opens. Its contents score, then move as each player’s single group to the chosen region, before the regions score. Lin therefore cannot wait to see Jo’s destination and then revise the choice. Rules pages 6–8
Lin sends two to Galicia and Mei sends one to Navarra. Bo has no castle Caballeros; set Bo’s disc to Toledo for this example. Change only Jo’s destination:
Jo chooses · Galicia after movement and its points · Navarra after movement and its points · Subtotal including the castle
Navarra · Lin 3, Jo 2: Lin scores 4, Jo 2 · Lin 1, Jo 3, Mei 2: Lin scores 1, Jo 5, Mei 3 · Lin 8, Jo 10, Mei 4, Bo 0
Galicia · Lin 3, Jo 4: Lin scores 2, Jo 4 · Lin 1, Jo 1, Mei 2: Lin scores 1, Jo 1, Mei 5 · Lin 6, Jo 8, Mei 6, Bo 0

Castle points are unchanged: Lin and Jo tie for the largest group and receive the second award, three each; Mei receives the third award, one. In the second branch’s Navarra, Lin and Jo tie behind Mei, so each receives the third award, one. An absent color earns nothing merely because a rank is unoccupied. Neither destination offers a King or Grande bonus here. Ties and bonuses, page 8

Jo’s switch takes the lead in Galicia away from Lin, yet lowers Jo’s subtotal from ten to eight. Mei changes no decision and rises from four to six. In multiplayer majority systems, effects can travel between places and players. A local victory is not a substitute for comparing the connected settlement. This still does not establish Jo’s best move for the whole game: future positioning and other scores have not been reduced to this little table.

The castle combines memory of publicly announced inputs with uncertainty about a newly hidden decision. Even perfect recall of the colors inside cannot reveal Jo’s disc. When designing a hidden-information component, decide separately what history is recoverable, what choice is still undisclosed and when commitment occurs. A transparent container might reduce memory demands without removing the destination decision. That is our proposed design experiment, not an official variant or an experiment the designers have reported.
Designer’s account: What survives a change of theme?

In a 2015 Brettspielbox interview, Kramer discusses finding a new theme after a competing Trojan Horse game appeared. He says that his and Ulrich’s mechanisms remained distinct, giving them a basis for further development with a Spanish setting. The author’s anecdote reproduced in the interview explicitly says both theme and system changed.

This supports a particular development history, not a claim that renaming components completes a retheme. It does not explain how our two King sequences were invented or provide results from testing a transparent castle. Keeping the record separate from our analysis lets us ask a useful further question: which roles, actions and relationships in a new setting help explain the rules, and which still need explicit explanation? Historical associations do not themselves grant permission to take an action.
Check your understanding, with answers
After recruiting two with card 9, can Lin deploy additional people straight from the Province? No. The Action card gives a ceiling; the available people still come from the Court.
Why do the King examples differ when both end with five deployed and the King in Galicia? The moment of the King’s move changes legal deployment targets. The two actions cannot be interleaved.
Does remembering every color’s castle count determine the regional scores? No. Destinations remain secret, and those groups arrive before regional scoring.
Does Jo’s lead in Galicia increase Jo’s three-location subtotal? No. It falls from ten to eight once the loss in Navarra is included.

Quacks：抽到安全筹码，为什么下一抽反而更危险？
手伸进袋子之前，玩家面对的并不是一个永远不变的“运气值”。已经抽走什么、还剩什么、愿意损失哪种收益，以及材料之间怎样接续，都会改变下一次决定。把这些关系拆开，才能看见《The Quacks of Quedlinburg》的设计不只是不断询问“还要不要再抽”。
本文使用 Schmidt 产品号88220的英文基本规则（官网文件名标为2024），无试管的锅板正面，以及第一套配方书（Set 1）。作者 Wolfgang Warsch 与版本出处可在出版社产品页核对。以下为本站构造的局部推演，不是作者访谈、实际试玩或最优策略证明。各局面的占卜事件已经处理，且没有效果改变所列袋中构成、位置、阈值或结算；不使用扩展、其他配方与末轮兑换规则。
角度一：风险跟着剩余的袋子走，损失则要分项算
先准备最初的九枚筹码：白1四枚、白2两枚、白3一枚、橙1一枚、绿1一枚。白筹的合计值超过7才爆锅，恰好7仍可停手。数字也用于沿锅内轨道前进，但彩色筹码不会增加白筹合计。规则第3—4页
林的水滴在起点0，没有鼠尾起步加成，药瓶尚未使用。已经依次抽出白2、白2、白1、白1，白筹合计6，最后一枚在第6格。袋中剩下五枚：白3、白1、白1、橙1、绿1。下面只计算“下一次普通盲抽立刻爆锅”的概率，假设充分混匀，每枚剩余筹码等可能抽到；不使用药瓶或其他效果。
目前状态 · 下一抽会爆锅的筹码 · 立刻爆锅概率
白值6，袋中仍是上述五枚 · 只有白3 · 1/5＝20%
先抽到橙1；白值仍是6，袋中余四枚 · 仍只有白3 · 1/4＝25%
从原状态先抽到一枚白1；白值变成7，袋中余四枚 · 白3与另外一枚白1 · 2/4＝50%
第三行剩余的白1只有一枚，不是两枚：刚抽出的那枚已经在锅里。计算危险筹码之前，必须同时更新分子与分母。这也说明，不能笼统地把“抽到白色”与“这次爆锅”画等号。
第二行尤其适合拿来检查设计直觉。橙筹这一次没有伤害林，却从袋中移走了一个安全选项。因此，在阈值没变的条件下，下一抽更危险。风险增加不一定来自玩家遭遇了坏结果，也可能来自安全结果已被用掉。反过来，新买的彩色筹码会改变以后袋子的构成，却不会让下一轮保证抽到它。

失败的代价也不是一句“这轮全没了”。另起一个仍用原始九筹袋的例子：林依次抽出白2、白2、白1、白1、白1、橙1、绿1、白3。最后白值为10，白3仍放到第12格，必须停止；结算看下一格，也就是印有13金币、2分和红宝石的格子。绿筹是倒数第二枚已放筹码，因此在 Set 1 中还提供一颗红宝石。即使爆锅，林仍获得这两颗红宝石，却不能参与奖励骰比较；这一次白3也不能用药瓶退回救场。结算与药瓶见规则第5—6页；绿筹见配方附录第3页
接着，林必须在该格的2分与13金币购买额度之间二选一。例如，只购买一枚价格10的蓝2，剩余3金币额度作废，并放弃这次格子上的2分；选择2分，则不能同时购买。这里的金币是本轮额度，不是可以存下来的现金。绿筹与格子给的红宝石另算，原有积分也没有被清除。
设计自己的冒险系统时，应逐项写下失败后保留什么、失去什么、还可选择什么。此处买材料与拿分的取舍，把一次爆锅连接到未来袋子的质量；但没有后续轮数、对手分数和购买目标，就不足以断言应当继续抽或一定选购买。
角度二：蓝筹买到的是一次选择机会，不是免疫
现在看另一场游戏的第2轮。林的袋子是原始九筹加一枚蓝2；这枚蓝筹已在上一轮合法支付10金币购买，没有其他增删。水滴仍在0，无鼠尾加成。林已依次放入白3、白2、白1、白1，白值7，再抽到蓝2并放在第9格。袋中此时剩下白2、白1、白1、橙1、绿1。
Set 1 的蓝2允许从袋中查看两枚，至多选一枚放入锅，其余退回；也可以全退。蓝筹自身的两格移动已经完成。这个“看见之后再决定”与连续盲抽两次不同。配方附录第1页，Crow skull／Set 1
把同值的两枚白1暂时编号，五枚里取两枚共有10组等可能的组合。其中三组都是白筹，六组一白一彩，一组是橙与绿。因此，有7/10＝70%的机会，林能看到至少一枚不会让白值增加的彩色筹码。其余3/10可以全部放回，蓝筹留在第9格，白值仍是7。
这不是“蓝筹仍有30%概率强制爆锅”。 查看本身不要求把危险筹码放入锅。若全退之后林选择停手，便没有这一抽导致的爆锅；若接着恢复普通盲抽，袋中仍是三白两彩，下一抽爆锅概率为3/5。
如果看到白2与绿1，林可以放绿1、把白2退回。此时锅前进一格，绿筹可能带来结算收益，袋中却变成白2、白1、白1、橙1：继续普通盲抽的爆锅概率升到3/4。蓝筹帮助选择安全的一次进展，没有消灭退回去的白筹，也没有给之后所有抽取提供保护。
对设计师而言，这是一种很具体的能力划分：增加一次可见选项，允许拒绝全部选项，与移除危险物，影响的是不同环节。若原型里都写成“降低风险”，玩家与设计者很容易误判持续时间。可以用相同剩余袋子，分别比较盲抽一枚、查看两枚选至多一枚、永久移除一枚白筹，记录各自改变了哪个决定；这些实验中自行新增或改写的规则，不能反过来当成原游戏的规则。
角度三：移除材料之后，为什么锅里的进展不倒退？
第三组局面从另一场游戏的第3轮开始。林的袋子只比初始袋多一枚黄1：第1轮没有购买，第2轮用8金币买入黄1。黄色配方从第2轮开放，因此这枚筹码的加入时点合法。水滴为0，无鼠尾加成；其余额外效果均不参与。
林依次抽到白2、白2、白1。三枚分别在第2、第4、第5格，白值为5。接着抽到黄1，先放到第6格；黄筹紧接着白筹，林可以把刚才的白1退回袋里。第5格留下空位，黄筹仍在第6格，白值变成4。配方附录第2页，Mandrake／Set 1
黄筹结算方式 · 锅中白值 · 最后筹码的位置 · 袋中剩余构成 · 下一次普通盲抽立刻爆锅
不用可选能力 · 5 · 第6格 · 白3、白1三枚、橙1、绿1 · 1/6
退回上一枚白1 · 4 · 第6格 · 白3、白1四枚、橙1、绿1 · 0/7
再让两条分支都抽到白3。它们都会前进到第9格：没有退白筹的分支白值变成8，爆锅；退过白筹的分支白值变成7，仍安全。安全分支并非从此无忧：此时袋中余四枚白1、橙1、绿1，继续普通盲抽的爆锅概率是4/6＝2/3。刚刚退回的白筹，仍可能在后面再出现。
这里有三份不能混为一谈的记录：锅里白筹的合计、末筹在轨道上的位置、袋中剩余内容。退一枚白筹改变前两者中的第一项，同时增加袋中数量；它不会把末筹往回拉。若把锅看作“现有材料面值的总和”，就无法解释第5格的空位与仍在第6格的黄筹。实体摆放保留了这次效果发生过的痕迹，帮助玩家区分已经推进的距离和当前承受的白值。
同样，永久移动水滴与本轮使用鼠尾也改变起步位置，却不等于更换袋子：水滴的推进能延续到以后，鼠标记在轮末收回，下一轮再按分差之间的鼠尾计算。规则第3、7页 这些是可分开调节的设计变量，不能只用“给落后者补偿”或“让材料更强”一笔带过。它们是否让某群玩家觉得公平，仍需要实际测试，本文没有这样的测量证据。
带答案的自查
第一张概率表中，白值6时先抽走橙1，为什么风险从20%变25%？危险的白3还在，安全筹少了一枚；分子不变，分母从5变4。
蓝2查看到两枚白筹，是否必须选一枚导致爆锅？不必，可以全部退回后停手；30%是没有安全选项的概率。
爆锅后用13金币额度中的10金币购买蓝2，还能拿这次格子上的2分吗？不能；但本例的绿筹与结算格红宝石照常获得。
黄筹把前一枚白1退袋后，为何最后位置仍为6？黄筹已经放好，其能力保留位置；白值下降，退回的白筹则重新成为以后可能抽到的内容。

Quacks: Why Can a Safe Chip Make the Next Draw More Dangerous?

Before reaching into the bag, a player faces more than an unchanging level of luck. What has already come out, what remains, which reward they can afford to lose, and how ingredients follow one another all change the next decision. Separating those relationships reveals more of The Quacks of Quedlinburg than the repeated question, “Shall I draw again?”

This article uses Schmidt product 88220, its English base rules in the official file named 2024, the pot side without test tubes, and ingredient Set 1. The publisher’s product page identifies Wolfgang Warsch and the rules source. The situations below are our own local thought experiments, not designer interviews, observed playtests, or proofs of optimal play. Fortune Teller effects have been resolved and do not alter the stated bag contents, positions, threshold, or settlement. Expansions, other ingredient sets, and final-round conversion rules are outside the examples.
Angle one: Risk follows the remaining bag; losses need separate accounts

Start with the original nine chips: four white 1s, two white 2s, one white 3, one orange 1, and one green 1. The pot explodes only when its white total exceeds 7; exactly 7 still allows a safe stop. Chip values also move ingredients along the pot, but colored chips do not increase the white total. Rules, pp.3–4

Lin’s droplet is at 0, with no rat-tail starting advantage and an unused flask. Lin has drawn white 2, white 2, white 1, white 1, in that order. The white total is 6 and the last chip occupies the sixth space. Five chips remain: white 3, white 1, white 1, orange 1, green 1. We calculate only the chance that the next ordinary blind draw immediately explodes. Assume thorough mixing and equal chances for each remaining chip, with no flask use or other effect.
Current situation · Chips that would immediately explode the pot · Probability
White total 6; the five chips listed above remain · Only white 3 · 1/5 = 20%
Orange 1 comes out first; white total remains 6, four chips remain · Still only white 3 · 1/4 = 25%
Instead, a white 1 comes out from the original situation; white total becomes 7, four chips remain · White 3 and the other white 1 · 2/4 = 50%

The third row has only one white 1 left, not two: the one just drawn is already in the pot. Both the numerator and denominator need updating before counting dangerous outcomes. Drawing white and exploding are not interchangeable events.

The second row is particularly useful for checking design intuition. The orange chip did no immediate harm, but removed a safe possibility from the bag. Without any threshold change, the next draw became more dangerous. Increasing risk can follow a good outcome because that safe result has been consumed. Conversely, buying a colored chip changes a future bag without guaranteeing that it will appear next round.

Failure also needs a more precise description than “lose the round.” Consider a separate situation using the same original nine-chip bag. Lin draws white 2, white 2, white 1, white 1, white 1, orange 1, green 1, then white 3. The white total reaches 10. The white 3 still goes on the twelfth space and drawing ends. The following scoring space displays 13 coins, 2 points, and a ruby. The green chip is the second-last chip placed, so Set 1 supplies another ruby. Lin receives both rubies despite the explosion but cannot compete for the Bonus Die. The flask cannot return the white 3 that caused the explosion. Rules, pp.5–6; green Set 1, Almanac p.3

Lin must then choose between the space’s 2 points and its 13-coin buying allowance. Buying only a blue 2 for 10, for example, loses the unused three-coin allowance and forfeits those 2 points. Taking the points rules out buying as well. Coins here are a current-round allowance, not saved cash. The two rubies are separate, and previously earned points are not erased.

When designing a risk system, list what failure preserves, removes, and still lets the player choose. Here, the choice between ingredients and points connects an explosion to the quality of future bags. Without specifying the remaining rounds, opponents’ scores, and intended purchases, however, we cannot conclude that drawing again or choosing shopping is always correct.
Angle two: A blue chip buys a choice, not immunity

Now consider round 2 of another game. Lin’s bag contains the original nine chips plus one blue 2, legally purchased for 10 coins in the previous round, with no other additions or removals. The droplet remains at 0 and no rat-tail advantage applies. Lin places white 3, white 2, white 1, white 1, reaching a white total of 7, then draws blue 2 and puts it on the ninth space. White 2, white 1, white 1, orange 1, and green 1 remain in the bag.

Set 1’s blue 2 allows Lin to inspect two chips and place at most one, returning the others. Returning both is also allowed. The blue chip’s own two-space advance has already happened. Choosing after seeing the possibilities differs from making two successive blind draws. Almanac p.1, Crow skull / Set 1

Temporarily label the identical white 1s separately. There are 10 equally likely two-chip combinations. Three contain only white chips, six contain one white and one colored chip, and one contains orange and green. Lin therefore has a 7/10, or 70%, chance of seeing at least one colored chip that will not increase the white total. In the other 3/10 of offers, Lin may return both, leaving blue on the ninth space and the white total at 7.

This is not a 30% chance of a forced explosion. Inspecting does not require placing an unsafe chip. Returning both and stopping avoids an explosion from that offer. Returning both and resuming ordinary blind draws leaves the original three-white, two-colored bag, with a 3/5 chance of exploding on the next draw.

If the offer is white 2 and green 1, Lin can place green and return white. The pot advances one space and the green chip may produce an evaluation reward. But the bag now contains white 2, white 1, white 1, and orange 1: the next ordinary blind draw explodes with probability 3/4. Blue helped Lin choose one safe advance. It neither destroyed the returned white chip nor protected all later draws.

For a designer, these are distinct abilities: adding a visible option, allowing all options to be rejected, and removing a dangerous object. Calling all three “risk reduction” hides where each acts and how long its benefit lasts. With the same remaining bag, a prototype experiment could compare a blind draw, inspecting two and placing at most one, and permanently removing a white chip. Record which decision each changes; invented experiment rules must not be mistaken for rules of the published game.
Angle three: Why does progress remain after an ingredient is removed?

The third situation begins in round 3 of a separate game. Lin’s bag has only one addition to the starting contents: yellow 1. Lin bought nothing in round 1 and paid 8 coins for yellow in round 2. Yellow becomes available in round 2, so that acquisition timing is legal. The droplet is at 0, with no rat-tail advantage or other relevant effects.

Lin draws white 2, white 2, white 1. They occupy the second, fourth, and fifth spaces, with a white total of 5. Yellow 1 comes next and first goes on the sixth space. Because yellow directly follows white, Lin may return that preceding white 1 to the bag. The fifth space becomes empty, yellow stays on the sixth, and the white total falls to 4. Almanac p.2, Mandrake / Set 1
Resolving yellow · White total · Last chip’s position · Remaining bag · Immediate explosion on the next ordinary draw
Decline the optional ability · 5 · Sixth space · White 3; three white 1s; orange 1; green 1 · 1/6
Return the preceding white 1 · 4 · Sixth space · White 3; four white 1s; orange 1; green 1 · 0/7

Now let both branches draw white 3. Both advance to the ninth space. Without the return, the white total becomes 8 and the pot explodes. With the return, it becomes 7 and remains safe. That safe branch is not safe forever: four white 1s, orange 1, and green 1 remain, so another ordinary draw explodes with probability 4/6 = 2/3. The returned chip can appear again.

Three records must stay distinct: the white total in the pot, the last chip’s track position, and the bag’s remaining contents. Returning white changes the first and adds to the bag, without pulling the last chip backward. Treating the pot as simply the sum of currently present chip values cannot explain the empty fifth space and yellow still on the sixth. Physical placement preserves a trace of the earlier effect, helping distinguish distance already gained from the current white total.

Similarly, permanent droplet movement and a round’s rat-tail advantage change where drawing starts without changing the bag. Droplet progress persists, while the rat stone comes out at round end and its next placement is recalculated from rat-tails between scores. Rules, pp.3 and 7 These are separate design variables, requiring more precision than “help the trailing player” or “make ingredients stronger.” Whether particular players experience them as fair remains a playtesting question; this article provides no such measurement.
Self-checks with answers

Why does drawing orange first increase the first table’s risk from 20% to 25%? The dangerous white 3 remains while a safe chip leaves; the numerator stays one and the denominator falls from five to four.
Must a blue 2 offer containing two white chips force an explosion? No. Both can be returned and the player can stop. The 30% figure describes offers without a safe chip.
After exploding, can Lin spend 10 of the 13-coin allowance on blue 2 and also take the space’s 2 points? No, but the green-chip and scoring-space rubies in this example are still received.

Why is the final position still six after yellow returns the preceding white 1? Yellow is already placed and its ability preserves that position. The white total falls, while the returned chip becomes a possible later draw again.

Ticket to Ride：牌凑齐了，为什么路还不一定修得成？
地图上的一格很便宜，却可能决定你要不要多花几轮绕路。一张七分车票也不只关系到“能否再加七分”：截止前接上最后一段，还会同时消除原来的负七分。
《Ticket to Ride》由 Alan R. Moon 设计。本文限定美国地图基础游戏，采用官方 2015 年英文重印规则：30张目的地车票，开局抽三张、至少留两张。官网现已同时提供新旧规则；2025 V2 的组件和初始发票方式有调整。这里不混用新版、Europe、USA 1910 或周年版规则。2015规则第2页；官网新旧规则入口
下面三组都是本站构造的独立二人局面，不是实际试玩或作者指定的解法。地图公开，手牌和车票按规则处理；为复算而列出的对手牌、暗牌顺序，不表示玩家可以预知。我们关注三种不同约束：空间还有没有位置、资源什么时候取得，以及取得之后还剩几次行动。
角度一：同一张地图，实际容量会随人数变化
先看达拉斯（Dallas）和休斯敦（Houston）。两城之间印着两条各一格的灰色线路。但在二、三人局中，一条被占，另一条就关闭；四、五人局允许不同玩家各占一条，同一玩家始终不能两条都占。规则第3页，Claiming Routes
设游戏刚开始，林先行动，乔随后。两人各有45辆列车，地图没有列车，线路分都是零。林的四张初始牌为两红、两蓝；乔为两绿、一黄、一白。这里只比较林希望让自己的线路连接达拉斯与休斯敦时的两条行动路径，不把这两个城市杜撰成一张目的地车票。
林可以立刻交一红，占一条灰线：花一辆、得一分，手牌余三张，完成眼前这次连接。如果林先抽牌，而乔随后交一黄占了其中一条，那么林下次即使牌更多，也不能使用另一条。
被关闭的是直连选项，并不是两座城市从地图上消失。若以下线路保持空闲，林可以另行收集牌，依次修出这条指定绕行：
线路 · 需要的列车／牌 · 该次铺线得分
Dallas → Little Rock · 2；任选同一颜色的一组 · 2
Little Rock → New Orleans · 3；绿色组 · 4
New Orleans → Houston · 2；任选同一颜色的一组 · 2
这条绕行共用七辆，至少要三个自己的铺线回合，得到八分；直连是一辆、一次铺线、一分。比如两蓝、三绿、两红可以支付表中三段，但林的初始四张牌还不够，收集缺牌的回合也得另算。我们没有证明它是所有局面中的最短或最优绕行，更没有假定乔会永远不碰这三段。官方地图跨第2—3页；计分表第4页
由此可以分开两笔账。多走六格确实多得到七点线路分，却也多用六辆列车、至少两次铺线行动，还可能改变后续车票的连接方式。不能只看分数增加，就认定绕行没有损失；也不能只看距离增加，就认定它对所有计划都更差。
这是一个直接的地图设计问题：图上画了几条线，与当前人数下允许几个人使用，是两件事。做自己的路线原型时，可以固定城市、长度和任务，只改变双线开放人数，记录玩家是在原地竞争、提前占位，还是改走旁路。本站提出这个对照实验，并不声称 Moon 当年就是这样测试的。
角度二：万能牌的价格，还包括取得它的方式和回合
再看洛杉矶（Los Angeles）到埃尔帕索（El Paso）的六格黑线。另一个刚进行过一轮抽牌的二人局里，地图仍空：林有五黑、一绿，共六张；乔有六黑。这个前序可以由两人各四黑开局，林先盲抽黑、绿，乔再盲抽黑、黑得到，尚未超出每种普通颜色十二张的牌量。
现在轮到林。公开五张为万能、红、蓝、黄、白；为了比较三条分支，固定暗牌堆顶依次为万能、黑。这个顺序对林未知，不能作为行动建议的前提。
林的抽法 · 实际拿到什么 · 回合结束时手牌
第一张拿公开万能 · 只拿这一张，不能再抽第二张 · 五黑、一绿、一万能，共7张
第一张拿公开红，补位亮出万能；第二张盲抽 · 第二张抽到黑；不能选公开的任一万能 · 六黑、一绿、一红，共8张
第一张盲抽到万能；第二张拿公开红 · 第二张之后补位亮出黑 · 五黑、一绿、一万能、一红，共8张
三支都足以组成六张黑色支付组；第一和第三支会用万能代替一黑。差别来自拿牌过程：明取万能占用整次抽牌行动，盲抽到万能仍只算其中一张。第二支新翻出的万能也不能作为第二张拿走。规则第3页，Train Car Cards
第三支拿得更多，不等于“盲抽总是赚一张”。它依赖我们固定的暗牌顺序；若顶牌换成白牌，同一次选择的所得就变了。第一支则事先知道一定能拿到万能。做资源获取设计时，应分别记录确定性、适用范围和数量，不要只给每张牌贴一个固定价格。
还缺一笔时间账。林这次选择了抽牌，不能接着在同一回合铺线。固定乔的下一步为交出六黑，占 Los Angeles—El Paso：乔剩39辆，立即得15分。无论林刚才走哪支，下一回合都不能再占那条已经属于乔的线路。林凑出的牌仍留在手里，可以寻找别的用途，但不会保留这条路的位置。
对设计师而言，这里可以检查“资源到手”和“执行承诺”是否发生在同一次行动。把二者分开，会让中间的对手回合有意义。公开手牌会让抢占风险更容易判断，却不会自动消除这段时间间隔；这也是信息规则与行动规则不能混为一谈的地方。
角度三：最后一个回合，把七分车票变成十四分的差距
第三个独立局面已经接近结束。林只铺过 Chicago—Saint Louis 的两格绿线，以及 Little Rock—New Orleans 的三格绿线；用了五辆，线路分为六，还剩40辆。林持有真实的 Chicago—New Orleans 七分车票，两块网络之间恰好缺 Saint Louis—Little Rock 的两格灰线，且该段尚未被占。
为了把时间窗口说清，乔并不是凭空“只剩一辆”。乔依次连接了下表整条西部路线；数字为各相邻城市间所用的列车数，其中平行线只用指定的一条。

林的最后行动 · 林的线路分 · Chicago—New Orleans 票的结算 · 这两项小计
交两蓝，铺 Saint Louis—Little Rock · 6＋2＝8 · 连通，加7 · 15
抽列车牌，地图不变 · 6 · 未连通，减7 · −1
差距是16：新短线的两分，加上这张票从负七变正七的十四分。这里不是把七分车票写成“实际面值十四”，而是在比较失败与完成两个结局。两支中林的其余车票没有纳入上表，所以这不是完整终分，也不能据此宣布谁获胜。乔的连续44辆远长于林最多七辆，最长线路奖金在这两支都归乔。
这个局面也不证明所有短线都比长线重要。若这张票已经通过别路完成，同样两格就不会再次改变它的结算；若还缺两段，两段各自再便宜，也不能在只剩一次铺线行动时一起补完。
对原型的启发是：资源库存不等于剩余机会。林还剩40辆、牌也够，却不能把“先抽、下次再修”延续到终局之后。设计结束条件时，可以把事件写成时间顺序，实际走完触发者、其他玩家和计分之间的行动，再看它是否给了你预期的补救窗口。
从作者的实际开发过程继续追问
Moon 在与 Mark Kaufmann 合写的回顾中说，他先写规则概要和地图，当天自测，数日后与朋友测试，随后数周还调整过线路、规则和车票。Kaufmann 另行讲述了发行阶段对年代感与名称的处理。这是两位参与者的回忆，不能由此推导每条线路的具体设计动机。《The History of Ticket To Ride》，印刷第6—7页
本站从中提出一个可执行的记录方法：地图版本变更时，把“换了哪条边”和“哪些目标因此变容易或困难”放在同一张表中；再单独记录名称、图像和时代设定如何影响读者理解。机制调整与呈现调整可以相互支持，但需要不同证据。测试者愿意再玩是有价值的反馈，仍不足以证明每条线路、每张车票或每个人数配置都已平衡。
带答案的自查
二人局中，乔占了 Dallas—Houston 的一条灰线，林能占另一条吗？不能；四、五人局才允许不同玩家分别占用两条。
林先拿红牌，补位翻出万能，能把它当第二张吗？不能；但盲抽得到万能仍只算一张。
为什么凑出六张黑色支付组，还不代表保住了 Los Angeles—El Paso？抽牌与铺线是不同回合的行动，乔可能先占。
最后一例短线只有两分，为什么指定两项结算差16？两分来自新线路，另外十四分来自那张票从−7变为＋7。
乔结束回合时剩三辆，会触发最后一轮吗？不会；阈值是剩0、1或2辆，且触发者也再行动一次。
